sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Radiative Forcing**: The measurement of the capacity of a gas or other forcing agent to affect the energy balance of the Earth-atmosphere system. Positive forcing warms the surface; negative forcing cools it.
• **Greenhouse Effect**: The process by which radiation from a planet's atmosphere warms the planet's surface to a temperature above what it would be without its atmosphere.
• **Albedo Effect**: The measure of the diffuse reflection of solar radiation out of the total solar radiation received by an astronomical body. Lower albedo (e.g., melting ice) leads to higher heat absorption.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Global Warming Potential (GWP) - A measure of how much energy the emissions of 1 ton of a gas will absorb over a given period of time, relative to the emissions of 1 ton of CO2.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Carbon Sequestration**: Biological (afforestation) and Geological (CCS) methods to capture CO2.
• **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**: India's 8-mission strategy to address climate mitigation and adaptation.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Climate finance gap, technology transfer barriers, and 'Common But Differentiated Responsibilities' (CBDR) disputes.
• **Solutions**: Circular economy, Green Hydrogen, and Nature-based Solutions (NbS).

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'M-C-N-F' (Major GHGs: Methane, CO2, Nitrous Oxide, Fluorinated gases).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Methane (Agriculture/Livestock), CO2 (Fossil Fuels), Nitrous Oxide (Fertilizers), Fluorinated gases (Refrigerants/Industrial).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Aerosols' as always warming. Note: While Black Carbon warms, Sulfate aerosols have a cooling effect by reflecting sunlight.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Anthropocene' to describe the current geological epoch where human activity is the dominant influence on climate.

keyTakeaways: Climate change is a result of both radiative forcing and feedback loops (e.g., ice-albedo feedback).
Anthropogenic factors are the primary drivers of current rapid warming, far exceeding natural cycles.
India's climate policy is balanced between developmental needs and global environmental commitments.
